column1: # The English for the name on the Location plate -- the banner that reads
# スルメ山 or 首都　ラングバウ across the top of the quest map. Hand-written; this
# The Japanese is the key, and the key is what the game's own table says: the
# build writes the English into a copy of archives/Rance10EX_v1_04/5_クエストデータ.x
# on the way past and leaves the file itself as the game shipped it. A name with
# no English keeps its Japanese, which is what the plate drew before this file
# existed. modules/PlaceNames.js and docs/place-names.md have the rest.
# Three rows have no English on purpose:
#   ランス城   is not a name here but a sentinel. QuestMapParamAccessor@PlaceName::get
#              compares the field against it and, where it matches, draws
#              RanceCastlePositionString instead -- ランス城空中, ＪＡＰＡＮ城, ランス砦
#              or ランス城, whichever the castle is at the time. English here
#              would freeze the plate on one of the four. Those literals live in
#              the .ain and are a separate job; docs/place-names.md says which.
#   −−−        is the game's own blank, three dashes rather than a word.
#   ？？？     and ？？？？ are the game withholding the name.
# The plate is 458 pixels wide, the name is centred in it at 32 pixels, and the
# word "Location" occupies the left 80. So a name past about 300 pixels starts to
# run over that label and one past 458 leaves the plate -- neither clips, and the
# build reports both rather than cutting anything. Fifty-five of the game's own
# names are already over the label, so crossing it is not by itself wrong.
